sources.title: The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA)
sources.program: Private health insurance; group and individual markets
sources.scope_note: Federal parity requirements; confirm applicability (plan type, market, state law) before modeling any rule. 2024 final rules (HHS/Labor/Treasury, 2024-09-09) and CAA-2021 NQTL comparative-analysis duty noted from page; linked regulations not yet read. Re-verified 2026-11-01: page content unchanged since 2026-10-14 (and 2026-10-12) — same 145-line text, same seven section headers, Fact Sheets & FAQs and Regulations and Guidance still empty. NEW page-level observation: the per-classification mechanics not covered by the earlier workbook scenes — the substantially-all/predominant test applied separately to six classifications, MH/SUD benefits required in all classifications where medical/surgical benefits are provided, cumulative financial requirements (deductibles, out-of-pocket limits) combining both benefit types within a classification, and scope/duration standards (geographic limits, facility-type limits, network adequacy) subject to NQTL parity. Consumer shipped 2026-11-01: WORKBOOK scene u1_p5b3_sixboxes ('Six Boxes, One Wallet'), lesson mh-parity-six-boxes, status source_review_required. Dated snapshot: docs/source-snapshots/cms-mh-parity-2026-11-01.md Re-verified live 2026-11-04: page UNCHANGED for the fourth consecutive check (2026-10-12, 2026-10-14, 2026-11-01, 2026-11-04) — same 145-line text, same seven section headers, Fact Sheets & FAQs and Regulations and Guidance still empty; still no last-updated stamp, so the check date remains the version. NEW page-level angle shipped as consumer: the non-mandate rule — MHPAEA does NOT require MH/SUD coverage, the ACA EHB requirement supplies coverage in non-grandfathered individual/small-group plans, MHPAEA applies to small-group plans only indirectly via EHB, small employer generally 1-50 (states may expand to 1-100), and some states may be stricter than federal law (not enumerated on the page). Consumer shipped 2026-11-04: WORKBOOK scene u1_p5b4_nomandate ('The Coverage the Law Does Not Require'), lesson mh-parity-no-mandate, status source_review_required. NEW page-level angle shipped as consumer: the law's timeline — MHPA 1996 limited large-group plans to no less favorable annual/lifetime dollar limits on mental-health benefits; MHPAEA 2008 preserved those protections and extended parity to substance use disorders plus financial requirements and treatment limitations; interim final regulation February 2, 2010; final regulation published November 13, 2013, effective January 13, 2014, generally applying to plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2014; CAA 2021 comparative-analysis duty with analyses available to the Departments or applicable State authorities on request beginning 45 days after enactment.
